papers.title: Engineering the 3D structure of organoids.
papers.abstract: Organoids form through the sel f-organizing capabilities of stem cells to produce a variety of differentiated cell and tissue types. Most organoid models, however, are limited in terms of the structure and function of the tissues that form, in part because it is difficult to regulate the cell type, arrangement, and cell-cell/cell-matrix interactions within these systems. In this article, we will discuss the engineering approaches to generate more complex organoids with improved function and translational relevance, as well as their advantages and disadvantages. Additionally, we will explore how biofabrication strategies can manipulate the cell composition, 3D organization, and scale-up of organoids, thus improving their utility for disease modeling, drug screening, and regenerative medicine applications.

summary_en.motivation: Current organoid models have limited structural and functional complexity due to difficulty in regulating cell arrangement and interactions.
summary_en.method: This review surveys biofabrication strategies to manipulate cell composition, 3D organization, and scale-up of organoids.
summary_en.result: The advantages and disadvantages of various engineering approaches are discussed, highlighting improved utility for disease modeling and drug screening.
summary_en.validation: No experimental validation is presented; the paper is a conceptual review.
